input.quote: 28.1 This Agreement is governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.
input.rationale: Section 28.1 imposes Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction, which is outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales) and is walk-away territory as a foreign law with exclusive foreign venue. It also directly conflicts with 28.2, which already grants exclusive jurisdiction to the state and federal courts in New York County with only a temporary injunctive relief carve-out (the preferred forum element, already met). The shortest cure is to change the governing law words in 28.1 to New York and delete the conflicting Singapore forum, leaving 28.2's venue and 28.3's escalation intact. No arbitration provision exists elsewhere in the Agreement.

mappings.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
mappings.quote: The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction, and each Party irrevocably submits to personal jurisdiction and waives any objection based on venue or inconvenient forum. Nothing prevents a Party from seeking temporary injunctive relief in another court with jurisdiction to protect confidential information or intellectual property.

proposal.summary: Replace Singapore governing law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction in 28.1 with New York law, relying on 28.2's existing New York County venue.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We replaced Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction with New York law, our preferred position, which also removes the conflict with the exclusive New York County venue already agreed in 28.2. Delaware, California, or England and Wales law with the corresponding courts would be acceptable fallbacks.
